guidance.opening:
一九二〇年秋，波士顿。你被一位房东约到他的事务所：他刚继承一栋老宅，房客住不久，他想见见你这个被请来帮忙的人。纸页和墨水味铺在桌上。

房东史蒂文·诺特把帽子搁到椅背上，朝你点点头。「地方空着，名声也坏了。我按天雇人，弄清楚里头到底怎么回事，好让人肯再住进去。你不是来听我抱怨的——我要的是能出门办事的人。」

他推开一叠租约，双手交叠，看着你。「先说说，你是谁？平时靠什么吃饭？随便讲讲就行。」
guidance.advice: Use only listed occupations. Era is 1920s Boston; skip Hacker as anachronistic unless the player insists and reframe as a telegraph/code clerk. Strong public fits for a landlord’s daylight hire: Journalist, Private Investigator, Police Detective, Police Officer, Lawyer, Librarian, Professor, Author, Antiquarian, Parapsychologist, Doctor of Medicine, Engineer, Clergy. Useful training: Library Use, History, Law, Fast Talk, Persuade, Spot Hidden, Listen, Psychology, Occult (optional flavor, not a reveal). Languages: English is assumed; Latin or Italian can be optional if the player wants paper or immigrant-neighborhood color—do not treat them as required. Belongings: notebook, fountain pen, street clothes, modest cash, pocket watch; a press card, PI license, or medical bag only if the occupation supports it. Public involvement: answering a notice or a referral to look into why a rental will not stay occupied—rumor only, no keys, pay, or accepted job yet. Optional ties (not facts): knew a former tenant socially, owes a favor to a landlord, writes about city housing, curious about local ghost stories. Ask motivation lightly in conversation; do not interview age or list a profession menu. Preserve uncertainty: neighbors talk, the last family left after a scare; do not name hidden causes.
guidance.handoff: The visitor is in Steven Knott’s Boston office in autumn 1920. Knott has stated he wants a day-hire to find out why his inherited house will not keep tenants and to restore its name; he has asked who the visitor is and how they earn a living. No commission accepted, no keys or cash given. Continue from this identity conversation into investigator setup, then return to the same meeting.
